description: Use GGML_LOG_DEBUG() for debug messages and configure the logger to print them only when rpc-server is started with --verbose. Make sure we log a debug message for every server function.

comments.body:
Note that this verbosity check is applied quite late, in the application logic. Inside `ggml` we would still always construct the log message string, regardless of the verbosity, which can have some impact in certain cases. It's better to gate all debug logs in the library with a debug flag. For example, here is how the Metal backend does it:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/7f766929ca8e8e01dcceb1c526ee584f7e5e1408/ggml/src/ggml-metal/ggml-metal-ops.cpp#L159-L183

In contrast, user code such as the examples and the tools don't need extra gating flags since the logger macros already do the check. For example here, this is already gated by the verbosity level and won't construct any strings of the log is not enabled:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/7f766929ca8e8e01dcceb1c526ee584f7e5e1408/tools/main/main.cpp#L909-L911
Thanks. The RPC server doesn't link `libcommon`, so I will go with the first option.

I have added `LOG_DBG()` similar to the one we have in the `common` lib and use it extensively in the `rpc_server` implementation. 

On the client side we still use `GGML_LOG_DEBUG()` for non-expensive logs.

I think it's better to keep this function as it is and read the verbosity level from an environment variable, for example `GGML_RPC_DEBUG`. The idea is to keep the API clean from verbosity/log related settings.

This way, in order to see the internal `ggml-rpc` debug logs, you can run:

```bash
GGML_RPC_DEBUG=1 rpc-server ... --verbose
```

> ```shell
> GGML_RPC_DEBUG=1 rpc-server ... --verbose
> ```

Why do we need both env variable and `--verbose` flag in this case? I am fine with using env variable but I don't see what `--verbose` is supposed to do in this case. Maybe set the environment variable?

Atm `--verbose` is redundant for `rpc-server` because the `rpc-server` has no verbose logging.

The convention in the rest of the tools is that `--verbose` enables verbosity for the tool-level logic. And if you additionally need extra debug logs from within `libllama` or `libggml` you control these with env variables. But these extra debug logs still require `--verbose` to be passed to the tool.
